query: What are best practices for drafting German survey instruments, vignettes and randomized-response items with cognitive pretesting for farmers?

response.query: What are best practices for drafting German survey instruments, vignettes and randomized-response items with cognitive pretesting for farmers?
response.answer: Best practices for drafting German survey instruments for farmers include clear, simple language, culturally relevant vignettes, and cognitive pretesting to refine questions. Use straightforward randomized-response items and pilot test with a small sample. Ensure cultural sensitivity and clarity in all materials.

results.title: AI assessment changes human behavior
results.content: In the AI (human) condition, we specified that the application would be assessed by an AI (a human) ([_SI Appendix_, section D](https://www.pnas.org/lookup/doi/10.1073/pnas.2425439122#supplementary-materials)). All studies offer consistent evidence for the AI assessment effect (_d_ ranges from 0.22 to 0.72; see [_SI Appendix_, sections F–I](https://www.pnas.org/lookup/doi/10.1073/pnas.2425439122#supplementary-materials)). As predicted, AI assessment led to more analytical task approaches (_M_ = 6.00) relative to human assessment (_M_ = 5.52; _t_(389) = 8.10, _P_< 0.001, _d_ = 0.41, 95% CI = [0.31, 0.50]; [Fig. 2 _B_](https://www.pnas.org/doi/10.1073/pnas.2425439122#fig02)). The AI assessment effect did not interact with participants’ beliefs about the required analytical and intuitive capabilities for the position they were assessed for ([_SI Appendix_, section L](https://www.pnas.org/lookup/doi/10.1073/pnas.2425439122#supplementary-materials)). Study 5a employed a “consider-the-opposite paradigm” ([31](https://www.pnas.org/doi/10.1073/pnas.2425439122#r31)) asking participants to think about their expectation regarding what the AI focuses on in its assessment and then consider the opposite of this initial belief about AI assessment. Although previous research on AI assessment has focused predominantly on outcomes for organizations and candidates ([_SI Appendix_, section B](https://www.pnas.org/lookup/doi/10.1073/pnas.2425439122#supplementary-materials)), it has largely neglected the possibility that people may behave differently under AI assessment.
